origin: copied from the accepted Workbench mockup, help table H, 2026-10-13

data.Plot type: Choose how to lay out the cells: two features, the PCA map, the UMAP or t-SNE map, or a violin per group.
data.Lasso: Drag a loop around cells to select them. Click without dragging to select one cell.
data.Density: Draw contour lines where cells are packed densely.
data.Removed: Show cells removed in earlier edits as hollow grey points. They cannot be selected.
data.Colour by: Colour the points by a tier, a group, border cells or any measured feature.
data.Scale: How feature values map to colours: Linear, Log, or Rank (even spread, the default).
data.Colours: The colour scale used for a feature.
data.Colours in viewer: Paint the cells in the napari viewer with the same colours as the plot.
data.Mark good: Mark every selected cell good. Maps and groups are kept.
data.Mark bad: Mark every selected cell bad. Maps and groups are kept.
data.Unmark: Return the selected cells to unassigned.
data.Clear: Deselect all cells. Marks are not changed.
data.Shape: A small histogram of the feature after its rescale.
data.Skew: How lopsided the values are. Arrow up-right: a long tail of large values; down-right: a long tail of small values.
data.Bell: Filled dot: the values look bell-shaped (small skew and ordinary tails).
data.Rescale: How the values are transformed before PCA, UMAP and grouping. Auto uses log for a long right tail and none for bounded or symmetric features.
data.Auto rescale: Set every feature’s rescale by the skew rule: log for right-skewed, none for bounded or symmetric.
data.Defaults: Tick the default feature set and set every rescale back to auto.
data.Gate: Drag a range on the histogram to select the cells whose value falls inside it.
data.Colour plot by this: Colour the plot by this feature.
data.Method (Map): PCA, or residual PCA, which first removes the effect of cell size from every feature.
data.Components: How many principal components to keep. UMAP, t-SNE and grouping start from these.
data.Scaling: Standard centres on the mean and divides by the spread; robust uses the median and MAD and is less pulled by outliers.
data.Clip extremes: Cap values more than this many spreads from the centre before PCA (winsorize).
data.Neighbours: How many nearby cells UMAP looks at. Larger values show broader structure.
data.Spacing: How tightly UMAP packs similar cells (min_dist). Smaller values give tighter clumps.
data.Start from: Compute from the PCA components or straight from the rescaled features.
data.Distance: How the difference between two cells is measured.
data.Perplexity: Roughly how many neighbours t-SNE balances for each cell.
data.Method (Groups): Leiden finds communities in a neighbour graph; HDBSCAN finds dense clumps and leaves stragglers unassigned; K-means and GMM split into a set number of groups.
data.Resolution: Leiden only. Higher values give more, smaller groups.
data.Smallest group: HDBSCAN only. Clumps smaller than this are left unassigned.
data.Seed: The random start. The same seed and settings always give the same groups.
data.Divider: Drag up or down to give the plot or the tabs more room. Double-click to reset.
